title: Module quiz: Structured output at the architect level

questions.stem: Scenario S6, structured data extraction. A 300-page contract is cut into chunks, and the per-chunk results are merged. Two chunks give different vendor names. Which merge rule fits?

options.text: Take the value from the later chunk
options.says: Ruled out because "A merge that always takes the last value or the longest is a guess presented as data".

options.text: Record both and send them for review
options.says: A disagreement between chunks is a conflict to record and review, and not a choice to make silently.

options.text: Take the longer of the two names
options.says: Ruled out because a later chunk with a different vendor is to be handled with "do not pick silently", and choosing the longer name is the same kind of pick.

options.text: Drop the field from the merged result
options.says: Ruled out because the rule is to record the clash "so that the document goes to review", and dropping the field hides it.

questions.stem: Scenario S6, structured data extraction. A team extracts invoice fields. Each failed extraction gets two more attempts. One failure is a currency written outside the allowed list, and another is a purchase order number that the document does not contain but downstream needs. Which handling is right?

options.text: Return the first with its error, review the second
options.says: The currency error is fixable by a second look and the missing number is absent from the source.

options.text: Return both with their errors until each is filled
options.says: Ruled out because for an absent value "No second look will find what is not there".
Ruled out because a format error is what feedback is for, since "The information is in the document; the form was wrong".

options.text: Review the first, return the second with a firmer prompt
options.says: Ruled out because it inverts the two, while "A required value that the model reports as absent is not retried".

origin.section: What a retry can and cannot fix

questions.stem: Scenario S6, structured data extraction. A team extracts invoice fields with a strict schema through a forced tool, and caches a long instruction block and a 200-page document. For some requests it switches `tool_choice` from `any` to `auto` and back, and costs run above plan. What explains it?

options.text: Each change also discards the stored tool definitions and the system prompt text
options.says: Ruled out because "Tool definitions and system prompts remain cached".

options.text: Moving between modes turns off structured output for the next request
options.says: Ruled out because the documented effect of a change is on the cache: "changing tool_choice between requests invalidates cached message blocks".

options.text: Each change discards stored conversation content, which is processed again
options.says: Changing the mode invalidates cached message blocks, so the content must be reprocessed.

options.text: Requests in automatic mode are billed at a higher rate than the others
options.says: Ruled out because the cost described is reprocessing, since a pipeline that alternates modes "pays to reprocess the document".

origin.section: Retries, conflicts, chunks, honest accuracy and the practice
